note: The why says what the drill trains and why it pays off, each block is the same drill turned a new way (find, name, every place), and done is a feel (no counting frets), never a count.

exercise.title: Notes on the low E and A strings
exercise.focus: Natural notes on the E and A strings · frets 0 to 12 · find, name, every place
exercise.why: The low E and A strings hold the root of almost every chord you will move up the neck, so knowing their notes lets you place any chord fast.

sections.text: Press Start in the game below. It names a note: find it on the low E or the A string and play it, saying its name out loud. Keep going until you stop counting frets from the open string.
Now the other way round: the game lights a fret and you name the note. Play it as you answer, so your hand learns the place while your eyes learn the name.
Play every place the named note sits on both strings, low to high. Then make up your own round: pick a note, find it on E, then on A, and step up to the next letter.
